choices.content: Completing just one of the steps is sufficient
The numbers of ways for the individual steps should be added
Every step must be completed in order for the task to be complete
The steps can be reversed into mutually exclusive categories

question.prompt: In which situation does the multiplication principle of counting apply?

solutions.explanation:
When a task is divided into steps, every step must be carried out. To multiply the step counts, the number of choices at each particular step must also be the same after every valid sequence of earlier choices. Provided the complete sequences represent all outcomes exactly once, the total number of ways is the product of the numbers of ways for the individual steps.

Requiring every step alone is insufficient. Suppose the first step has two choices: one allows exactly one continuation at the second step, while the other allows exactly two. Both steps are required, but these disjoint cases cover all outcomes and give \(1+2=3\) ways. There is no single second-step count to multiply by \(2\).

Thus C is the intended choice if the usual fixed-count condition is understood. As written, C omits that condition, so none of the options states a complete sufficient condition.
solutions.title: Recognize the required steps and check the counting condition
